title: Вердикт комиссии и транс Макса  (The Commission's Verdict and Max's Trance)

segments.t: At the commission's dinner table, the chairwoman declares that Hotel Eleon deserves only three stars because the service is a nightmare. To win a vote in their favor, Chef Barinov sits behind the unconscious Pavel Vladimirovich and puppets his head while the hypnotist puts Max into a trance.
Мой вердикт — три звезды.
Сервис, персонал — это кошмар какой-то!
Кому ещё вина?
Вкусно. Павел Владимирович, а вы что думаете?
Понятно. Я, конечно, согласен с вами.
Но с другой стороны, в целом отель неплохой.
Персонал старается.
Я сейчас.
Всё понравилось?
Очень.
Что-то он долго. Она его в транс вводит!
Ничего, Макс с детства не поддаётся гипнозу.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Мой вердикт — три звезды.
'My verdict is three stars.' Explaining that his verdict is three stars lays the cards on the table for Barinov.
Сервис, персонал — это кошмар какой-то!

'The service, the staff, it is some kind of nightmare!' Insisting that the service the staff it is some kind of nightmare shows the inspector is not backing down. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
Кому ещё вина?

'More wine for anyone?' Over the favor and the hotel, Mikhail presses Barinov for a straight answer. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Вкусно. Павел Владимирович, а вы что думаете?
'Delicious. Pavel Vladimirovich, and what do you think?' Wondering if Pavel Vladimirovich and what do Barinov thinks shows the inspector caught off guard.
Понятно. Я, конечно, согласен с вами.

'Understood. I, of course, agree with you.' Between the work and the favor, Barinov gives the inspector a quick, grounded response. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Но с другой стороны, в целом отель неплохой.
'But on the other hand, overall the hotel is not bad.' Claiming that on the other hand overall the hotel is not bad sounds confident, even if the inspector has doubts.
Персонал старается.
'The staff tries hard.' Noting that the staff tries hard keeps Barinov's side of the story simple and clear.
Я сейчас.
'I will be right back.' Even though he will be right back, Mikhail keeps a steady face in front of Barinov.
Всё понравилось?

'Did you like everything?' By asking whether the inspector likes everything, Barinov presses the inspector for a straight answer. In Russian, he does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question.
Очень.
'Very much.' Between the hotel and the table, the inspector gives Barinov a quick, grounded response.
Что-то он долго. Она его в транс вводит!

'He is taking a long time. She is putting him into a trance!' Once he is taking a long time, Mikhail makes sure Barinov hears every word. Russian puts the key word right up front so his emotion lands on the first beat.
Ничего, Макс с детства не поддаётся гипнозу.

'It is nothing, Max has not succumbed to hypnosis since childhood.' Adding that it is nothing Max has not succumbed to hypnosis since childhood fills in the missing piece for the inspector. Russian stacks "never" or "nothing" together with "not", doubling the refusal for extra weight. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Мой вердикт — три звезды.
Сервис, персонал — это кошмар какой-то!
Кому ещё вина?
Вкусно. Павел Владимирович, а вы что думаете?
Понятно. Я, конечно, согласен с вами.
Но с другой стороны, в целом отель неплохой.
Персонал старается.
Я сейчас.
Всё понравилось?
Очень.
Что-то он долго. Она его в транс вводит!
Ничего, Макс с детства не поддаётся гипнозу.
That brings the dining-room scene to a close. Notice how the chairwoman announces her three-star verdict while Kostya realizes the woman is putting Max into a trance. See you next time!
До завтра!
